results.name: How to Customize Your Shop's Appearance
results.title: How to Customize Your Shop's Appearance
results.body:
You can define your brand and show buyers what makes your shop unique by customizing your shop’s appearance. To give your shop more visibility, use creative elements like banners, strategically arrange the items of your shop, and feature items you want to showcase to buyers.

Learn more about size requirements for images in your Etsy shop.

  • How to customize your shop banner 
  • How to edit your order receipt banner
  • How to add a logo
  • How to arrange the items in your shop
  • How to feature items

Sellers can get a three-month Adobe Express Premium plan trial to help create professional-looking images for your Etsy shop.

Reach out to Adobe's support team if you need any assistance using their services.

How to customize your shop banner
 

Shop banners are the largest branding asset for your shop. This image appears when shoppers view your shop on the standard view of the website as well as on mobile devices.

To add your shop banners:

  1. On Etsy.com, go to your Shop Manager.
  2. Select the pencil icon next to your shop name under Sales Channels.
  3. Select Banner to showcase your brand and listings at the top of the page. 
  4. Choose the type of banner you want. 
  5. Choose Done.

You have 2 styles of banner to choose from: 

  • Mini Banner: A narrow image with a minimum size of 1200 x 160 pixels.
  • Big Banner: A large image with a minimum size of 1200 x 300 pixels.

If you do not want a banner for your shop, select None. This will move your listings higher up on the page and your logo will be the most prominent branding on your shop homepage. 

More advanced shop banner options, such as the Carousel banner or Collage banner, are available to Etsy Plus subscribers. 

How to edit your order receipt banner

You can personalize the receipts buyers receive when ordering from your shop by adding a custom banner to them.

To manage your order receipt banner:

  1. On Etsy.com, go to your Shop Manager.
  2. Choose Settings.
  3. Choose Info & Appearance.
  4. Select Choose file next to Order receipt banner.

How to add a logo

Adding a logo helps visually represent your shop, your brand, and what you sell. It’s prominently displayed at the top of your shop for buyers to see.

To add or edit a logo: 

  1. On Etsy.com, go to your Shop Manager. 
  2. Select Settings, then select Your shop.
  3. Under Logo, select Add to add a logo or Edit to edit your logo.
  4. To add a logo, select Add file or drag and drop your file.
  5. Select the square (crop) icon to crop your image. Select the x to remove your image.
  6. Select Save.

You can also add or edit your logo in your Shop home visual editor, which can be found by going to Sales Channels in your Shop Manager and selecting the pencil icon next to your shop name. You can also access your Shop home visual editor within Your shop settings.

A good logo should: 

  • Reflect your shop’s personality 
  • Look good both big and small 
  • Use simple graphics or illustrations 
  • Keep any text short and easy to read 
  • Avoid long words or busy backgrounds

Your shop should have a logo to represent your business to buyers. Not having a logo may impact your visibility in Etsy search.

How to arrange items in your shop 

Thoughtfully arranging the order of items in your shop is a great way to entice shoppers to browse your products. Much like a display in a physical shop, the way your products are arranged in your Etsy shop can make a big impression about your brand. 

To rearrange items in your shop:

  1. On Etsy.com, go to your Shop Manager. 
  2. Select Settings, then select Your shop.
  3. Under Listing order, select Edit.
  4. Choose which listings are shown first in your shop. Select Custom or Most recent.
  5. Select  Save.

If you select Custom, you'll need to set the order of your listings using your Shop home visual editor. Your Shop home visual editor can be found by going to Sales Channels in your Shop Manager and selecting the pencil icon next to your shop name. You can also access your Shop home visual editor within Your shop settings. Select Rearrange items.

To move listings between pages, select the Move to page dropdown menu on the individual listing. 

When listings are renewed, they'll go back to their custom location. New listings go to the top of your shop.

It could take up to 10 minutes for your listings to rearrange on your public shop homepage.

Tips for arranging your products in your shop:

  • Be cohesive with imagery and style.
  • Update arrangements seasonally to reflect shopping trends.
  • Keep a full shop to avoid looking sparse. 
  • Use the best thumbnail image for each product. 

How to feature items 

Featuring items is a way to showcase 4 listings you especially want shoppers to see when they visit your public shop homepage.

These items will appear just above your shop announcement.

A buyer can choose the listing image in the featured row or in its place with the rest of your items to get to the same listing page.

To feature your items: 

  1. On Etsy.com, go to your Shop Manager.
  2. Choose Listings.
  3. Select the star icon on the four listings you want to feature. You can only feature active listings. Choosing more than four items adds them to a queue so they'll be displayed if the items before them get removed from your shop.
  4. In the Listing status sidebar menu, find Featured listings and select Manage. 
  5. Drag and drop the listings in the order you want them displayed. 
  6. Select Done. 

The changes you make will take effect in your shop immediately.

results.name: How to Use the Etsy Search Visibility Page
results.title: How to Use the Etsy Search Visibility Page
results.body:
When shoppers are searching for items on Etsy, it’s important that they can easily find quality listings from shops they can trust. While there are many factors that impact an item’s placement in Etsy search, the Etsy search visibility page shows personalized shop insights and actions that can help how you show up in search. 

What is the Etsy search visibility dashboard?

The Etsy search visibility page in Shop Manager shows how your shop is performing in three key areas that can impact your placement in Etsy search:  

  • Your listings
  • Your shop 
  • Your customer service

The dashboard also shows recommended actions which may help increase your item’s search visibility. 

Your listings

Creating high-quality and clear listings helps buyers feel more confident making a purchase. Active listings need to meet certain requirements for a chance to receive priority placement in relevant search results, such as:

  • Has at least one listing image 
     
  • The listing’s primary photo contains high-resolution images (we recommend a width and height of 2000 pixels or more)

     
  • The listing’s primary photo is a singular image of a finished product (no collaged or stitched together images)
     
  • The primary photo is clear and well-lit
     
  • The listing’s category is as specific as possible
     
  • The listing has a return policy, even if it’s “No returns”
     
  • US listings with domestic shipping prices lower than $6 will be prioritized in search

If your listing is falling short in one or more of these areas, its visibility in search may be impacted. Both the Etsy search visibility page and your Listings manager show what improvements can help improve a listing’s search placement. Learn how to edit a listing.

The Etsy Seller app has tools to adjust listing photos.

Your listing titles 

At this time, title recommendations are only available to shops with their language set to English. If your titles already adhere to our guidance, the tool will not be visible. 

You may have access to an optional tool on the search visibility page that provides title recommendations. These recommendations are informed by Etsy’s guidance for writing clear titles. 

Go to the search visibility page and select Update titles to review, edit, and approve new listing titles. 

Before you make any updates, download a CSV of your listings. Use it to reference keywords from original titles and add them to your tags, descriptions, and attributes as you see fit. Learn more about keywords.

Your shop

Having a fully set up shop can boost buyer trust. Your shop should have a logo, which helps the buyer understand who you are. If your shop is not complete, your listings’ search visibility may be impacted. 

Learn how to add a logo to your shop.  

Your customer service

There are minimums that you must reach when it comes to customer service including: 

  • Responding to buyer messages in a timely manner
  • Shipping orders on time and with tracking
  • Maintaining a positive review score
  • Avoiding a high number of cases.

The Customer service stats page in Shop Manager details how you are performing in each key area and we’ll let you know if the service you’re providing to buyers needs some attention. Meeting these standards can help you avoid lower visibility in Etsy search. Learn more about Etsy’s Customer service standards. 

In some cases, repeat violations of these standards may result in temporary or permanent suspension of your selling privileges on Etsy. However, if you consistently go above and beyond these standards, you can earn a Star Seller badge.

Making search visibility improvements

The Etsy search visibility page will show you how your listings are performing in the areas of your shop, listing, and customer service quality. Once improvements have been made, the insights will typically disappear within 24 hours. 

You can filter through all of your listings to quickly see which search improvements can be made from your Listings page. 

To filter your listings for search improvements: 

  1. In your Shop Manager, go to Listings. 
  2. In the Search factors bar, filter by search visibility issues.  
  3. All listings with the selected issue will be displayed. 

We’ll let you know if the customer service you’re providing to buyers needs some attention in your Customer service stats. 

Changes can take up to one day to reflect in search. There are several other factors that impact where your listing shows up in search for any individual keyword, including keyword relevance and any search filters buyers may apply.

You can find more education on this in the Etsy search visibility page, and  How Etsy Search Works for an in-depth guide. Abide by Etsy policies to ensure that your listings can continue to show up or be sold on Etsy.

Learn more about our customer service standards.

results.name: Etsy Fee Basics
results.title: Etsy Fee Basics
results.body:
When you sell on Etsy, there are a few fees related to listing and selling an item.

The fees most sellers will need to know are:

  • Listing fees
  • Transaction fees
  • Payment processing fees

If you use Etsy tools such as Etsy Ads or Offsite Ads, or if you purchase shipping labels on Etsy, there are additional fees associated with those services. Learn more about fees and taxes for selling on Etsy. 

To view your Payment account, which includes fees and taxes you incurred from selling on Etsy:

  1. Sign in and choose Shop Manager on Etsy.com, or choose More on the Etsy Seller app.
  2. Select Finances.
  3. Choose Payment account.

If you have an Amount due, you can select Pay now, or use auto-billing if you’re in the US.

Listing Fees

When you add a product to your Etsy shop, we call this a listing. Listing fees are the fees you pay to list products for sale on Etsy. You’ll be charged a listing fee for each individual listing you post. 

The listing fee is a flat rate charge of $0.20 USD per listing. This fee is charged regardless of whether or not the item listed sells. The fee is automatically added to your payment account when you publish an item.

Other types of listing fees include auto-renew sold, multi-quantity, and custom listing fees.

Auto-renew sold fees

Auto-renewed listings automatically repost a listing if it’s purchased from your shop, saving you the time of manually reposting products. If you setup a listing to auto-renew and it’s purchased, you’ll be charged the standard $0.20 USD listing fee. 

Multi-quantity listing fees

If you have variations of an item for sale in a single listing and a customer purchases more than one variation, you’ll also be charged the standard $0.20 USD listing fee for each additional item purchased from the listing. The additional charges won’t post until a multi-quantity purchase has been made. 

For example, if you had more than one item in stock for a particular listing, and a customer purchases two different variations of that item, your payment account would reflect the original $0.20 USD listing fee plus an additional $0.20 USD for the additional item purchased. 

Learn more about multi-quantity listing fees.

Custom listing fees

Custom listings are useful when you want to post a particular product for a private sale to a particular buyer. Custom listing fees cost the $0.20 USD standard fee. 

Transaction fees

Transaction fees are the fees Etsy collects when a customer makes a purchase from your shop. Unlike listing fees, transaction fees are only collected on listings that sell. 

Transaction fee basics:

  • Etsy charges 6.5% of the total order amount in your designated listing currency.
  • This fee applies to the total cost of the item, along with shipping and gift wrap (if you charge your customers for those). You will see the charges itemized separately on your Payment account.
  • The transaction fee amount posts automatically to your Payment account.

Payment processing fees

Payment processing fees are a set rate plus a percent of the total sale price of the item. This rate and percent vary by country. The fees are taken from the item’s total sale price, including its shipping fees, and any applicable sales tax.

Payment processing fees are charged on each transaction that uses Etsy Payments. These processing fees appear in your payment account and are deducted prior to deposit. They are in addition to Etsy's transaction fees. 

Learn more about payment processing fees.

results.name: India Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020
results.title: India Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020
results.body:
The Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 (the “Rules”) are intended to prevent unfair trade practices in e-commerce for consumers in India. These rules apply to e-commerce entities that offer goods or services to consumers in India, including marketplaces like Etsy.

Jump to a section:
  • What is Etsy?
  • How do the Rules impact Indian consumers?
  • How does Etsy comply with the Rules?

What is Etsy?

Etsy is a global marketplace for unique and creative goods. Etsy is made up of individual third­-party sellers who run their own shops, create their own policies, and are responsible for their inventory, shipments, and complying with the law. We provide a venue, but Etsy does not manufacture goods, hold physical inventory, or ship items on behalf of our third-party sellers. The content uploaded on Etsy's marketplace is generated by independent sellers, who are not employees, agents, or representatives of Etsy.

How do the Rules impact Indian consumers?

Buyers located in India are welcome to use our existing channels to contact us about any concerns they have through Etsy’s Help Center, which will allow Etsy to most efficiently address any issues. 

For additional support, Etsy has an appointed Grievance Officer for India consumer outreach. 

EtsyStore Private Limited
B583, Adjacent Park Plaza, Gurgaon In, Sushant Lok PH1, Gurgaon, Haryana, India 122001

Email: grievanceofficer@etsy.com

Buyers based in India (along with any other members who live outside of North and South America) contract with Etsy Ireland UC, a subsidiary of Etsy, Inc. when using Etsy. The contact information for Etsy Ireland UC can be found on Etsy’s Legal Imprint. 

Etsy, Inc.’s headquarters are located at:

117 Adams Street

Brooklyn, NY 11238.

India consumers with questions about a seller’s listing content or shop practices may feel free to directly contact the seller through Etsy Messages. 

How does Etsy comply with the Rules?

Etsy complies with the Rules through its existing policies and procedures, as summarized below:

  • Sellers on Etsy must accurately represent their items in listings and listing photos, respect the intellectual property of others, and may not coordinate pricing with other sellers.
  • By listing a product for sale on Etsy, sellers agree that they are responsible for complying with all applicable laws and regulations, including requirements regarding labeling, disclosures, and fair pricing. 
  • Etsy’s Anti-Discrimination and Hate Speech Policy prohibits the use of our Services to engage in discrimination.
  • Sellers may not engage in shilling (falsely inflating their review scores), or otherwise undermine the integrity of Etsy’s reviews system.
  • If a seller is unable to complete an order, they must notify the buyer and cancel the order.
  • Buyers can request that a seller provide a return or exchange or can choose to open a case against a seller.
  • Sellers must disclose their geolocation, such as the location of their shop or the country they ship from. 

To contact the Grievance Officer’s team for additional help, click Contact support below.

results.name: What is the "Star Seller" Badge?
results.title: What is the "Star Seller" Badge?
results.body:
Quick answer

Star Seller eligibility is reviewed on the 1st of every month. If you meet the criteria, it may take up to 24 hours for your badge to appear.

Learn more about how to track your progress toward becoming a Star Seller.

The Star Seller badge is our way of recognizing sellers with a proven record of providing stellar customer service. When you become a Star Seller, we show buyers the badge on your shop, so they know you go above and beyond for your customers.

Star Seller eligibility is reviewed on the 1st of every month based on your customer service stats over the past 3 months. 

To be eligible to become a Star Seller you need to first meet our minimum customer service standards for case rate, and have certain order and sales criteria. Learn more about how Star Seller metrics compare to customer service standards.

You also need to meet higher standards for message response rate, on-time shipping & tracking, and average review ratings:

  • Message response rate: reply to 95% of first messages in a thread within 24 hours
  • On-time shipping & tracking: 95% of orders ship on time, with valid tracking or a shipping label purchased on Etsy (when required) 
  • Average review ratings: 4.8+

Learn more about how to track your progress toward becoming a Star Seller.

If you have feedback about Star Seller, please let us know by filling out our survey.  

Read more about Star Seller in our Star Seller Terms and Conditions.

How your shop is evaluated for the Star Seller badge

You’re eligible to become a Star Seller starting 90 days after your first sale – as long as you’ve met our customer service standards for the month, and received at least 5 orders and $300 in sales over the past 3 months.

How often will my shop be evaluated? 

Star Seller eligibility is reviewed on the 1st of every month. It may take up to 24 hours for your badge to appear on your shop and Star Seller dashboard.

The default view on your Customer service stats page shows your performance for the current review period, which updates daily and reflects progress toward next month’s badge. To see the review period used to determine your current badge, toggle to the previous review period tab.

What time period is my shop being evaluated for?

When evaluating shops for Star Seller, we look at the last 3 months of data prior to the review date.

Does a Star Seller badge affect my search ranking?

Star Seller badges do not directly impact your search ranking. However, Star Seller badges make it easier for buyers to identify and shop from Star Sellers. Learn more about how search works. 

Will my shop be impacted if I'm not a Star Seller? 

If you're not a Star Seller, you won’t be penalized. However, we expect sellers to uphold the customer service expectations in our Service Level Standards. Consistently not meeting these standards may impact your search visibility, and shop or account status.

You can learn more about specific ways to improve how to deliver an excellent customer experience in your Customer service stats. 

If you don’t see a Star Seller badge on your shop

If you’ve confirmed that you’ve met the Star Seller criteria  but you don’t have a badge on your shop, it’s possible your shop doesn’t comply with all of Etsy’s policies. To become a Star Seller, your shop must also comply with all of Etsy’s policies.

I had a Star Seller badge, but it’s been removed

If your shop earned a Star Seller badge or individual badges, but no longer meets the requirements for the program, we may remove them. In accordance with the Star Seller Terms, the following may result in temporary or permanent disqualification from the program:

  • Your shop no longer meets the qualification criteria.
  • Your shop has an overdue bill.
  • Your account privileges were limited.
  • Your account violated our Terms of Use, including and not limited to our Seller Policy.
  • We have reason to believe you attempted to falsely inflate your Star Seller stats.

If your Star Seller badge was removed because of an overdue bill, you may be able to reinstate your Star Seller badge by paying your bill.

Learn more about why a Star Seller badge may be removed.

The Star Seller badge is our way of recognizing sellers with a proven record of providing a great customer service. To become a Star Seller, your shop must meet certain criteria for messages, shipping, ratings, orders, and sales. Learn more about the Star Seller badge.

If you have feedback about Star Seller, let us know in this survey.

If you meet the criteria to receive a Star Seller badge after an evaluation period, it can take up to 24 hours for the badge to be displayed. 

Messages, shipping, ratings, orders, and sales are calculated to determine Star Seller status. In order to be evaluated, you need to have been on Etsy’s platform for 90 days since your first sale.

The Message response rate only applies to the first message in a conversation. Initial messages from both buyers and sellers on Etsy are counted toward the Message response rate. Messages sent through temporary or recurring weekly auto-replies also count toward Message response rate. 

You can see your Star Seller status from your Star Seller dashboard: 

  1. Sign in to Etsy.com and go to Shop Manager.
  2. Select the Customer service stats tab. 

On this dashboard, you can track your progress across 5 areas related to the customer experience. You can also track your progress toward earning individual customer service badges for message response rate, on-time shipping, and excellent reviews from here. 

The default view on your Customer service stats page shows your performance for the current review period, which updates daily and reflects progress toward next month’s badge. To see the review period used to determine your current badge, toggle to the previous review period tab.

results.body:
To purchase Evri shipping labels through Etsy, you must be based in the UK and accept either Etsy Payments or Paypal.  

What shipping services are available? 

Recent changes to US trade policies could result in large customs fees and halted shipments. In response, we’ve temporarily suspended the purchase and use of shipping labels on Etsy through Evri with a US destination. Learn more.

For sending items within the UK, you can choose: 

  • Shop to Home Standard
  • Shop to Home Next Day

For international services, use Evri Parcelshop Standard. 

To track your parcel, go to Evri’s website and manually enter the 16-digit tracking number. If you enter a tracking number for an international parcel, you’ll be redirected to Evri’s Globo Eco website. 

Sellers also have the option of dropping off packages with an Evri label at any one of their local ParcelShop locations or by using one of Evri's parcel Lockers. 

Learn more about what can and cannot be sent in the mail.

How much do shipping labels cost? 

The cost of a shipping label will depend on the origin, destination, weight, and dimensions of the package. There are no additional fees from Etsy to use Evri shipping labels outside Etsy’s normal fees (i.e. transaction fees).

When purchasing an Evri shipping label on Etsy, you can preview its cost after you add the package details. The cost of each purchased shipping label will appear separately in your account. 

VAT is not charged on Evri postage purchased from Etsy.

How do refunds and claims work? 

To request a refund

If you bought a label by accident or no longer need it, you can request a refund for unused, unscanned Evri labels less than 15 days old.

You can purchase a new label at a later time. Learn how to request a refund for a shipping label.

To file a claim for lost or damaged items

For orders that were lost during transit or damaged in the mail, use the Evri Help Centre to file a claim via the chat bot. Be prepared to provide the tracking number for your package, with a description of your lost item enquiry or of any damage caused to the item. You have 28 days from the package’s scheduled arrival date to file a claim for lost or damaged items.

results.name: How to Comply with US CPSC eFiling Requirements
results.title: How to Comply with US CPSC eFiling Requirements
results.body:
Quick answer

If you import certain consumer products into the US, you may need to electronically submit product safety certificate information to the US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) before your shipment arrives. 

In this article:

  • What is eFiling?
  • How do I comply?
  • What products typically require a certificate?
  • Frequently asked questions
  • Additional resources

What is eFiling?

eFiling is a program run by the US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). Starting July 8, 2026, importers of certain consumer products will be required to submit product safety compliance information electronically before those products can enter the United States.

In the US, many products must meet specific safety standards. Products that are subject to a mandatory CPSC safety requirement need a certificate that confirms they meet that standard:

  • Children’s products require a Children’s Product Certificate (CPC)
  • Some other consumer products require a General Certificate of Conformity (GCC)

Previously, importers only needed to make them available upon request. The eFiling requirement means that key information from these certificates must now be submitted as part of the import process. If required eFiling information isn’t submitted, your shipment may be delayed, held for inspection, or stopped at the border. In some cases, products may be refused entry into the US.

If you manufacture your products in the United States, you are not required to eFile, though you still need to prepare these certificates and provide them upon request.

The CPSC usually considers products “finished” at the time they’re imported—even if you plan to decorate, personalize, or customize them later—if they could be sold as-is.

How do I comply?

If your product is subject to a CPSC safety requirement, you’ll need to submit information from your CPC or GCC as part of the import process. There are 2 ways to do this: 

  1. Work with a customs broker: A customs broker is a licensed professional who helps importers navigate US customs requirements. You can provide your broker with the required certificate information and they will submit it as part of your import documentation. Note that brokers may charge a fee for this service.
  2. Use the CPSC Product Registry: The CPSC Product Registry allows you to register your product and receive a reference ID, which you then include with your shipment’s customs information. If you use a postal or express carrier such as DHL, FedEx, or UPS, check with your carrier about how to provide this ID during the shipping or customs process. If you import by postal mail, this option is required.

You can register at the CPSC Product Registry. You may be able to reuse a reference ID for the same product for up to one year, provided the product has not changed.

Plan ahead. Give yourself enough time to register and gather your certificate information before importing products into the US.

What products typically require a certificate?

Children’s products almost always require a CPC when imported. This includes items such as toys, children’s clothing and accessories, furniture intended for children, and similar products. For other consumer products, requirements vary depending on the product type. The CPSC’s Regulatory Robot tool can help you identify whether a specific product is subject to a mandatory safety rule.

For children’s products, testing must be conducted by a CPSC-approved laboratory. A list of approved labs is available on the CPSC website.

Frequently asked questions

eFiling information is submitted as part of your import documentation, before your shipment arrives in the United States. If you’re working with a customs broker, they will handle this as part of the entry process.

If required eFiling information isn’t submitted, your shipment may be delayed, held for inspection, or stopped at the border. In some cases, products may be refused entry into the US.

A customs broker is a licensed professional who helps importers submit documentation and comply with US import requirements. While not required, sellers may choose to work with a broker to help manage the process.

Additional resources

  • CPSC guidance and resources
  • CPSC list of approved laboratories

results.name: What To Do if Etsy Puts Your Shop in Vacation Mode
results.title: What To Do if Etsy Puts Your Shop in Vacation Mode
results.body:
Quick answer:

If Etsy puts your shop in Vacation Mode, it usually means there's an issue with your account that needs to be resolved before you can continue selling. You cannot turn off Vacation Mode for your shop when setting is enabled by Etsy. In most cases, Etsy will automatically turn off Vacation Mode once any account-related issues are resolved. If the restriction remains and your account is eligible, you may be able to file an appeal through the Appeals Center.

In this article:

  • Why Etsy put your shop in Vacation Mode
  • What happens when Etsy puts your shop in Vacation Mode
  • How to get Etsy-initiated Vacation Mode turned off
  • Frequently asked questions
  • Additional resources

Why Etsy put your shop in Vacation Mode

Check for an email from Etsy or a notification in Shop Manager for information specific to your shop. Common reasons Etsy may place your shop in Vacation Mode include:

  • Missing or outdated taxpayer information
  • Payoneer verification issues
  • Policy violations or issues with listings
  • Account security concerns
  • High case rate or falling below Etsy’s customer service standards
  • Location-based restrictions

What happens when Etsy puts your shop in Vacation Mode

Vacation Mode does not pause shop responsibilities or recurring fees. You remain responsible for fulfilling open orders, resolving open cases, responding to buyer messages, and paying recurring subscription charges. 

When Etsy places your shop in Vacation Mode, most of the same features, limitations, and fee rules apply as when you turn it on yourself. However, there are a few important differences:

  • You cannot turn off Vacation Mode yourself.
  • Etsy may automatically turn off Vacation Mode after you complete any required task(s) and resolve any account-related issues.
  • Active Etsy Plus and Pattern subscriptions will be paused automatically--you will not be billed during the pause.
  • You will not be charged renewal fees for listings set to auto-renew.
  • Your Star Seller badges will not be visible on your shop's homepage while your shop is paused. If you violated Etsy's policies or your shop performance falls below eligibility thresholds during the pause, you may lose your badges permanently.

How to get Etsy-initiated Vacation Mode turned off

Start with these steps to identify and resolve the issue:  

  • Check the email Etsy sent about your shop status and follow the directions in the message.
  • Open Shop Manager and look for a red or yellow alert banner. Review and complete any required actions. 
  • Navigate to your Finances page and check for any errors or action items with your legal and taxpayer information or your bank account information. 
  • If your legal and taxpayer information or bank account information is pending verification, Vacation Mode may remain on until Etsy completes the review.
  • Check your customer service stats to see if you are falling below any standards and work to resolve any delayed shipments, open cases or order issues before reaching out to support. Learn more about Etsy’s Customer Service Standards.

If your shop is connected to Payoneer:

  • Confirm that your Payoneer account information matches your Etsy account information and make updates as needed. 
  • Check your Payoneer account for pending tasks. Payoneer will review your submission and contact you if further action is needed. Shop suspensions are typically lifted within 24–48 hours after resolving your Payoneer issues. Learn more about using a Payoneer Account with Etsy Payments.

If your shop is eligible for an appeal, you’ll have the option to submit an appeal through Etsy’s Appeals Center. 

Frequently asked questions

Can I turn off Vacation Mode myself if Etsy turned it on?

No. When Etsy places your shop in Vacation Mode, only Etsy can remove the restriction after the required issue is resolved.

Can I submit an appeal to have Vacation Mode turned off?

If your shop is eligible for an appeal, you’ll see the option to submit an official appeal form through the Appeals Center. 

Why does Payoneer say I’m verified while Etsy still shows a problem?

Etsy and Payoneer may show different statuses if verification data has not synchronized or if Etsy still needs matching account details. Check that your name, business name, address, tax details, and identity documents match across both accounts. Contact Payoneer support and request that they refresh the connection on their end.

Additional resources

  • How to Complete Orders if Your Shop is Closed or Suspended
  • How Do I Use a Payoneer Account With Etsy Payments?
  • What are Etsy's Customer Service Standards?

results.name: What is Etsy's Purchase Protection for Sellers?
results.title: What is Etsy's Purchase Protection for Sellers?
results.body:
If an order is eligible for Etsy Purchase Protection, Etsy will cover up to $250 of a refund (or the converted equivalent in your local currency), and any remaining amount will be charged to the seller. You won’t need to issue the refund yourself. Etsy Purchase Protection may apply in the following situations:

  • A buyer never received their package (for example, if it was lost in transit)
  • Their item arrived 7+ days after its estimated delivery date window provided at checkout
  • Their item arrived damaged (for the first instance per calendar year)
  • Their item matches the listing description and photos, but a buyer claims it does not

To make sure your orders are eligible for Etsy Purchase Protection, you’ll need to follow the eligibility criteria outlined in our Etsy Purchase Protection for Sellers and remain in good standing with Etsy, and meet our customer service standards. 

For cases opened prior to May 7, 2026, refer to the Etsy Purchase Protection policy in effect at that time.

What isn’t eligible for Etsy’s Purchase Protection program? 

The following situations will make an order ineligible for Purchase Protection:  

  • The order does not meet one or more of the eligibility requirements for Etsy Purchase Protection.
  • The item doesn’t match the listing description. We strongly recommend using accurate photos and descriptions when listing an item.
  • You obtain insurance from a third-party source, or have carrier and/or payment processor coverage. We ask that you first submit a claim to your primary source of coverage instead. 
  • Your shop is not in good standing for violating Etsy policies.

Sellers are responsible for refunding costs for orders that fall outside of these eligibility requirements.

See our article of best shipping practices to ensure you’re following the proper steps for your order to arrive undamaged. 

Buyers are responsible for paying any customs duties, import duties, or other charges imposed by their country's government, payable on delivery. Items that arrive late or are not received due to buyer delay or refusal to pay charges owed upon delivery, do not qualify under Etsy's Purchase Protection Program. In this instance, sellers are not responsible for refunds but may offer them at their discretion.

How do I qualify for Etsy Purchase Protection? 

Etsy Purchase Protection will automatically cover qualifying orders with no setup required from the seller.  

The Etsy Purchase Protection process only begins after:

  1. A buyer reaches out to you about an order through a Help request
  2. The buyer opens a case about the order

Once a buyer has taken both of these actions, Etsy will review the order and make a resolution. If the order is eligible for Purchase Protection, Etsy will refund the buyer, and you’ll keep your earnings from the sale.

Our guide to case resolution gives an in-depth breakdown on how the case system works, and the steps that should be taken to manage buyer issues. 

Orders are eligible for Etsy’s Purchase Protection program if: 

  • The order was shipped within your stated processing time
  • Valid tracking was provided and/or it was mailed out with a shipping label purchased through Etsy
  • Your listing has an estimated delivery date, which includes transit times and, where applicable, an origin zip code
  • The item received by the buyer matches the photos and description on your listing
  • You meet Etsy’s customer service standards
  • You responded to the buyer’s Help with Order message within 48 hours
  • It is the first instance in the calendar year of an item arriving damaged
  • Duties and import fees are included upfront if the order is shipping into the US

If an order meets these requirements, Etsy will cover up to $250 (or the converted equivalent in your local currency) of the refund amount, even if the order total exceeds $250. Sellers are responsible for refunding costs for orders that don’t qualify for Etsy Purchase Protection.

In addition to these requirements, you must ship orders on time and provide tracking when available. Etsy may also use carrier tracking scans, in addition to sellers marking the order as shipped and uploading valid tracking, to confirm that an order was shipped on time.

To help protect the full order value, consider purchasing shipping insurance for orders over $250.

In some situations, a specialist may need to reach out for more information about the order. It’s important that you respond to requests for information in the case log within the time frame given to show both the buyer and Etsy that you are working towards a solution.

Etsy Purchase Protection continues to evolve to better support sellers. Your feedback helps shape how the program improves over time. Share your thoughts in our survey.

If you still have questions about a closed case for an item that arrived damaged or different than described, you can reach out to us to dispute the outcome.

How it works

  1. Share what happened on the next page. The more specific you are, the better we’ll be able to help.
  2. A trained specialist will review your case and outcome to make sure everything aligns with Etsy’s policies and Etsy’s Purchase Protection program. 
  3. You’ll get a final decision via email within 1-3 business days.

Item arrived damaged or different 

Generally speaking, if your case was about an item that the buyer never received or arrived 7+ days after its estimated delivery window provided at checkout, we can’t review your outcome further since we already have all the info we need. For more help with these cases, check what’s eligible for the Etsy’s Purchase Protection program or read our tips on shipping orders.

Item never received 

If your case is still open, you’ll need to go to your Shop Manager to communicate directly with the buyer in your case log.

results.name: How do I Set Return Policies on My Listings
results.title: How do I Set Return Policies on My Listings
results.body:
Setting return policies on your listings clearly displays important information to your buyers, including:

  • Which items from your shop can be returned or exchanged, if any
  • The time frame that you accept returns and exchanges

You can set different return and exchange policies for each physical listing you sell in your Etsy shop, or set one specific policy across all your physical listings. Buyers will see your return policies when viewing your listings. If you’re a seller outside of the EU, you must set a return policy whenever you edit or create a new listing for a physical item, even if it is to let buyers know you do not accept returns or exchanges on that listing. Not having a return policy may result in your listings appearing lower in Etsy search. Learn more about Etsy’s Customer service standards. 

If you want to set store-wide policies for things like your cancellation and privacy policies, you can do this through your shop policies. 

Jump to a section:

  • How do I set return and exchange policies on my listings? 
  • How do I change a listing’s return policy?
  • How do I use a simple return policy?
  • Do I need to accept returns or exchanges? 
  • Can digital downloads be returned?
  • How can I accept returns for items where customization is optional? 

How do I set return and exchange policies on my listings? 

When creating or managing your listings, you have the option to create a new return policy, or to choose from one of your existing policies if you have any. We also have a simple policy template that you can choose instead of creating your own. You can also create and/or apply policies to multiple listings at once in Listings Manager.

To create a return and exchange policy through Policy settings:

  1. Go to your Shop Manager. 
  2. Navigate to Settings.
  3. Select Policy settings.
  4. Navigate to Returns and exchanges.
  5. Select the Create Policy button.
  6. Choose whether you accept returns and/or exchanges for that item by selecting the checkmark next to each option. 
  7. Select the time frame that you’ll accept returns and exchanges for that item from the dropdown menu.
  8. Select Save and apply. 
  9. Select Publish. 

If you’ve created at least one policy in the past, a suggestion to use the policy you’ve set the most on your active listings will be shown. Select Apply, or select Choose another policy to either pick from your other existing policies or create a new one.

Once a policy has been created, it can only be deleted if it is not associated with any of your active listings. 

How do I change a listing’s return policy?

To change the policy you currently have applied to a listing:

  1. Go to your Shop Manager. 
  2. Select Listings. 
  3. Select the listing whose policy you want to change.
  4. Navigate to Returns and exchanges. 
  5. Select the Change Policy button.
  6. Select from one of your other existing policies. The listing’s current policy is displayed as Applied. 
  7. If you want to create a new policy instead, choose the Create Policy button. 

You can also apply a return policy to multiple listings at once through your Listings Manager:

  1. Go to your Shop Manager.
  2. Select Listings.
  3. Select the listing(s) whose policy you want to change.
  4. Select Editing options.
  5. Select Change return & exchange policies.
  6. Apply an existing policy, or select Create policy to create a new policy. 

How do I use a simple return policy? 

If you choose to use the simple return policy template, the following settings are applied to your listing:

  • Buyers can return or exchange the item.
  • Buyers must return it within 30 days of delivery.
  • Buyers are responsible for any return shipping costs.* 
  • Buyers are responsible for any loss in value (as agreed upon with you) if an item isn’t returned in its original condition.* 

Choose this option by selecting Apply simple policy in the listing editor. When you are satisfied with your listing, select Publish.  

* These settings are standard on all returns and not specific to the simple return policy. 

Do I need to accept returns or exchanges? 

If you’re a seller outside of the EU, all of your physical item listings must have a return policy set so buyers know what to expect when purchasing from you. However, whether you choose to accept returns or exchanges on your listings or not is completely optional and based on your individual business needs. Not having a return policy - even if that policy is “no returns accepted” - may result in your listings appearing lower in Etsy search results. 

Consumer protection laws in the EU require some sellers to offer a minimum 14-day return policy on orders that ship to those countries. For additional information on this, review this help article on EU law regarding returns and exchanges. 

Can digital downloads be returned? 

It’s not possible to set return or exchange policies on your digital listings. If a buyer contacts you about an issue with a digital item they’ve purchased, you can still choose to resolve the issue as you see fit.  

How can I accept returns for items where customization is optional? 

If you offer an item in your shop that a buyer can choose to either purchase as-is or to customize, but only want to accept returns for non-customized or personalized orders, you can let buyers know in the FAQ section of your shop. You can also mention this in the relevant listing descriptions.

To edit your shop's FAQ:

  1. Go to your Shop Manager
  2. Select the pencil icon next to your shop name under Sales Channels. 
  3. Under Frequently asked questions, choose Add an FAQ. 
  4. Select Custom and personalized orders from the drop down. 
  5. In the Answers text box, specify that you do not accept returns of customized or personalized orders. 
  6. Select Save. 

You can also edit your Messages to Buyers to let shoppers know that you do not accept returns for customized or personalized items. Message to Buyers are included on order receipt pages and in the email buyers receive when they purchase from your shop.
